The paper establishes an analytical method for studying the electromagnetic wave interactions with a general radially anisotropic cloak.
A novel class of spherical nonlinear cloaks is derived, and their invisibility performance is examined using the proposed scattering method.
The general cloaking condition is proposed for the first time, relating the evolution operator of the cloak shell to the impedance tensor of the equivalent homogeneous air sphere.
Increasing the number of homogeneous layers 'N' used to discretize the anisotropic cloak shell from 10 to 100 improves the accuracy of the calculations.
An optimal range of the nonlinearity parameter 'x' around 2 is identified, where the NTB cloak outperforms Pendry's linear spherical cloak in terms of reduced scattering cross-section.
The transverse permittivity of the NTB cloak exhibits a non-monotonic behavior along the radial direction within the optimal range of 'x', which is the key to its improved invisibility.
The paper's general scattering algorithm can handle arbitrary radial-dependent anisotropic parameters (ε₊, μ₊, ε₋, μ₋) of the spherical shell.
The proposed NTB spherical cloak can achieve better invisibility performance compared to Pendry's linear cloak by optimizing the nonlinearity parameter 'x'.
The critical material singularity in Pendry's cloak is transformed into a less demanding geometrical singularity in the NTB cloak.
The NTB cloak's improved invisibility is attributed to the non-monotonic transverse permittivity profile, which is different from the monotonic behavior in Pendry's linear cloak.
The paper demonstrates that there exists an optimal range of the nonlinearity parameter 'x' where the NTB cloak outperforms the classic linear spherical cloak.
Discretizing the anisotropic cloak shell into 50 homogeneous layers is found to provide a good balance between accuracy and computational complexity.
The paper's general scattering algorithm can be applied to study the electromagnetic interactions with arbitrary radially anisotropic spherical particles.
The proposed NTB spherical cloak design offers a promising approach to achieve improved invisibility performance compared to the traditional linear cloaks.
The paper's findings suggest that carefully engineering the nonlinearity in the transformation function can lead to enhanced cloaking capabilities.
